newsitem.title: FRANCE: Tietmeyer says believes EMU will start on time.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer says believes EMU will start on time.

text.p: Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer said in an interview published on Wednesday that European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) would start on time in 1999, barring surprises.

"There are strong reasons to believe today that the timetable will be respected, at least by a limited number of countries, as foreseen in the Maastricht treaty," the German central bank chief told the afternoon daily Le Monde.
"I start from the principle that if nothing surprising happens between now and then, monetary union will begin at the start of 1999," he said.
He added that he would welcome Italy's participation as a founder of EMU as long as it met Maastricht treaty criteria in a lasting way.
"Italy is undertaking considerable efforts to resolve its problems and that is positive," he told Le Monde.

"If Italy fulfils the criteria in a lasting way, it will of course be welcome in the community of the euro. We must not point the finger at this or that country but rather we take note with pleasure that all countries are making great efforts to fulfil the required conditions."
